messages.subject: Access Raw Data
parts:
Hi, 

Is there a way I can access or create an excel file containing the raw mz and corresponding intensity values for a mass spectrometry file I have opened using cardinals readAnalyze function? I have tried using spectra() however my columns are all 0s and I cannot view more than 6 columns and rows. 

Thanks, 
Shriya

messages.author: db2a70d9b31cb1f7
messages.subject: Re: Access Raw Data
parts:
Hi Shriya,

the spectra() function should be valid. You can check the dimension of your loaded dataset by using dim().

This is the code I use to get the raw data matrix as txt file:

msidata_matrix = as.matrix(iData(msidata))

mz_names = paste0("mz_", mz(msidata))
pixel_names = paste0("xy_", coord(msidata)$x, "_", coord(msidata)$y)

 write.table(rbind(c("mz_name", pixel_names), cbind(mz_names, msidata_matrix)), ##create matrix
                    file="intensity_matrix.txt", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names=FALSE, sep = "\t")

Best,
Melanie

Hi Melanie, 

Thank you so much. So I just wanted to clarify, are the intensity values obtained by Cardinal a measure of intensity for each mz value at each pixel? Is there a way for me to obtain the intensity values for the average mass spectra of all the pixels. Meaning I would obtain an average intensity value for each mz? I have used the following code: 

readMSIData("C:/Users/Shriya/Downloads/mse.img") ###Import  mass spectrometry data from region 1
folder=setwd("C:/Users/ Shriya/Downloads/")
name="mse"
mse<-readAnalyze(name, folder = getwd(), attach.only = TRUE,as = "MSImagingExperiment") #Mass spectrometry data from region 1
plot(mse)
image(mse)
msidata_matrix = as.matrix(iData(mse))
mz_names = paste0("mz_", mz(mse))
pixel_names = paste0("xy_", coord(mse)$x, "_", coord(mse)$y)
write.csv(rbind(c("mz_name", pixel_names), cbind(mz_names, msidata_matrix)), ##create matrix
                    file="intensity_matrix.csv", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names=FALSE, sep = "\t")





Thanks, 
Shriya

messages.author: db2a70d9b31cb1f7
messages.subject: Re: Access Raw Data
parts:
Dear Shriya,

yes with spectra() or iData() you obtain a table in which each line is one mz feature and each column one pixel and the content of the table are the intensities per mz feature and pixel.

You can find the code for obtaining an average mass spectra in section 6.5 of the user guide: http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/Cardinal/inst/doc/Cardinal-2-guide.html#summarization-e.g.-mean-spectra

Cheers,
Melanie
